parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file sits in the application layer, but it defines the HTTP request-body contract. Its own doc comment calls `CancelOrderBodyDto` "The transport contract for POST /orders/:id/cancel", and it uses class-validator `@IsString()` decorators to validate the incoming request body. That makes it presentation/transport work, which belongs to the infrastructure layer (presentation/controller). The application-level command shape `CancelOrderDto` is also built by extending this HTTP body class, so the use-case input inherits the transport contract and its validation. The comment says the controller merges in the path id, which ties the use-case input to how the HTTP route is laid out. On their own, DTO files with validation decorators are a common pattern and a borderline case. Here, though, the code states plainly that it is tied to a specific route, so the transport responsibility is misplaced.
